# Lane 2.238: the guard at start reads the fence itself

## Builders 1 and 2, and the first fix round, 2026-11-26 (shortened)

- **What exists.** `checkLoginRole` (`packages/database/src/db/check-login-role.ts`), run by the website, the worker, `probe-logins` and `npm run test:real-postgres`, ends with `checkFence` (`check-fence.ts`), signature unchanged. It refuses, each with one mending statement: (a) a league table (a `league_id` column, the table one points at, or one the catalog lists, whatever its columns: missing, column gone or renamed, T-470) not enabled and forced; (b) a policy on one not the migrations' own word for word; (c) an unreviewed security-definer function the login or a role it may become can run (`reviewed-definers.ts`, 9, T-469); (d) a relation no migration made in their schemas, or readable by the login elsewhere (T-476).
- **The catalog (T-468).** `migration-catalog.ts`, generated by `npm run db:types` with the guard's own queries (`fence-catalog.ts`); `migration-catalog-file.test.ts` fails when stale.
- **Tests.** Embedded `check-fence.test.ts`; real server `fence-guard.test.ts` (plants by the tables' owner, read AS app_login, each shown to leak before it is refused). Policies printed on 16.15 equal PGlite's 17. Every check was broken by hand once and its tests failed.
- **Needs the founder (for STATUS):** in a session the founder started, the lead starts the website once against the test copy and reads any sentence naming a function in Supabase's own schemas, then revokes it or reviews it in.

## Second fix round (the look's Highs A, B, C and the Low), 2026-11-26

- **High A (T-481).** The catalog now lists every table, view, materialized view, foreign table and sequence the migrations made with its kind, owner and, for a view, a sha256 of its definition and options (none today; extension members left out). The guard refuses a listed one missing, of another kind (`drop view …, then run the migrations' own definition again`), of another owner (`alter table … owner to postgres`) or definition.
- **High B (T-477 widened).** All 55 functions in the migrations' schemas (not from an extension) are in the catalog: body hash, settings, owner, language, security, volatility. Missing or changed is refused by name; a non-definer says "a function the migrations made".
- **Low.** A catalog policy missing from a league table that is there is named with its `create policy … as permissive for … to … using (…) with check (…)`; that statement puts it back on both servers.
- **High C (T-482).** `library-schemas.ts` (beside `reviewed-definers.ts`) lists `pgboss` with its reason and the step-2.112 sentence. There, a relation with no league column whose view reads no league table is let be; one that does is refused with `revoke select …`, never `drop`. T-60 not changed.
- **Record 053's shape today.** The release: role `queue_owner` (no login, no powers), schema `pgboss` owned by it, `revoke all on schema pgboss from public`, `queue_owner` granted to the worker's login, never to the website's. Before this change and after it, the worker's first start passes (no pg-boss table yet); every later start of a login that reaches `queue_owner` is refused by T-60 alone: `app_login owns tables (pgboss.… and 12 more) … reassign owned by app_login to postgres`, and after a `reassign owned by app_login to queue_owner`: `app_login may become queue_owner, which owns tables …: revoke queue_owner from app_login`. Now no sentence says to drop pg-boss's tables (asserted in `start-up-certificate.test.ts`). **For the lead:** a worker start cannot pass in that shape without weakening T-60 (its login must make tables in `pgboss`, so it owns them or may become their owner); it was not weakened; step 2.112 solves it. Also spec and code already disagree here: T4's T-60 line says the worker's login may change the job library's schema; `checkLoginRole` refuses it. A website with its own login (no `queue_owner`) should pass; not tried, the test server has one login.
- **Tests.** Embedded (`check-fence.test.ts`, 26): accounts moved away with a view in its place; accounts replaced by a same-name table of another owner; `current_league_id` body and volatility, `current_account_id`, `require_view_of_every_league`; a missing function (a catalog listing one more); a league column dropped with cascade and made again; pgboss let be, its league table and view refused without "drop". Real server: `fence-guard.test.ts` +5 (the two accounts plants, the login seeing both leagues; `current_league_id` returning league B, the login set to A seeing B's programs; the other two functions; a dropped policy) and the release-shape test.
- **Breaks by hand.** Embedded, one at a time: relations check off; functions to reviewed only; volatility not compared; missing policies off; library list off; a library view's league read off; missing function not named: each failed its own tests only. Real server, all four main breaks at once: exactly the 6 new tests failed. A stale catalog (one volatility edited) failed `migration-catalog-file.test.ts`.
- **A fault of the first fix round, fixed.** `probe-logins.test.ts` failed at `2f823bf3` too: the guard's `to_regclass` of a listed table needs the use of its schema, so a login without it got "permission denied for schema public" instead of its sentence. Listed tables are now found by name in the catalog.
- **Run, passed.** `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`; `npx vitest run packages/database/src/db packages/database/src/isolation apps/worker apps/web/src/server/startup.test.ts` (32 files, 577); `packages/database/src/seed`, `league-making`, `schema/app-role.test.ts` (23 files, 191); `npm run test:real-postgres` whole (9 files, 70); the pending-decisions test (11, count unchanged). Not run: `npm run verify`, browser tests.
- **Time on the real server, nothing planted:** 16 to 41 ms per guard call (21 calls; opening the connection 37 ms apart).
- **Distrust.** A listed table replaced by a same-name table of the SAME owner is not seen (columns are not compared). `require_view_of_every_league` changed to do nothing is refused, but a definer calling it is not re-read. View hashes are untested across 16 and 17 (the migrations make no view).
